answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. A raven-like system ensures that only one identity can claim a task, while others are left in the shadows. The kernel of the system relies on cryptographic proof to show conflicting commitments signed for the same task. This ivory-tusked approach ensures the integrity of the system, preventing malicious actors from exploiting the bonds for personal gain.
